correctness.rationale: For each leader-pair orbit the follower subspace splits into within-part zero-sum modes of original degree d_i and a constant-on-parts quotient. If f_j followers remain in part j, the quotient has diagonal d_i and off-diagonal -f_j. This gives an independent determinant calculation against the frozen resolvent proof. If P(z)=a+bz+cz²+…, its contribution to J₂ is (b/a)²-2c/a and to J₁ is b/a. Replayed all four rational gap identities, coefficientwise positivity at m=3+h, the minimum formula, the values 1/2 and 187/300, and the four J₁ gaps at m=3. At m=2 for BB the empty B part contributes no modes: a formal dummy factor z+d_B cancels before evaluation. The five orbits exhaust the two-element sets since U is a singleton. Exact independent replay: python3 /workspace/check-3.py (SymPy). The submitted verifier was inspected, not executed.

value.rationale: The graph family already has a natural two-site first-inverse design rule. This all-m squared-inverse classification locates precisely where that rule changes: disjoint optimal orbits already on K_{1,3,4}, with no ties or missed competitor types. It is an exact comparison across the family, not merely an isolated numerical ranking. It claims neither a universal order rule nor equivalence to traditional first-order variance.
